beethoven_late_sketchbook.name: beethoven_late_sketchbook
beethoven_late_sketchbook.description: Late Beethoven pocket sketchbook (1824-1826) with heavy blotted quill and soft pencil strokes, slash noteheads, wild barline overshoot, extreme cramming and wobble, and heavy bleed-through.
beethoven_late_sketchbook.paleography_notes: Modeled on Beethoven's late string-quartet pocket sketchbooks (e.g., Kullak, de Roda, Autograph 11/2): folded rag-paper leaves carried on walks, combining blunted iron-gall quill and smudged graphite, degraded diagonal slash noteheads, violent cross-outs, extreme end-of-bar cramming, wavering hand-drawn/warped staves, and dense verbal marginalia.

schubert_rapid_lieder_draft.name: schubert_rapid_lieder_draft
schubert_rapid_lieder_draft.description: Franz Schubert's rapid single-sitting song draft on oblong Viennese paper with compact dense staves, forward-leaning cursive stems, rapid hooked rests, and closely packed bars.
schubert_rapid_lieder_draft.paleography_notes: Reflects Schubert's spontaneous Viennese Lieder drafts (e.g., Erlkonig, Winterreise working manuscripts): oblong rag-paper bifolia filled stave-to-stave with fluid warm iron-gall ink, strong rightward cursive momentum, compact rounded noteheads, rapid backwards-7 hooked quarter rests, and brisk dip-and-fade quill strokes.

schumann_cramped_diary.name: schumann_cramped_diary
schumann_cramped_diary.description: Robert Schumann's small, tight, upright-to-backslanted ink hand with compact noteheads, cramped spacing, fine pointed steel nib, and dense personal revisions.
schumann_cramped_diary.paleography_notes: Draws on Schumann's Leipzig and Dresden Skizzenbucher and Lieder diaries: fine pointed steel-nib strokes, unusually small compact noteheads, upright-to-backslanted stems, tight horizontal packing in dense polyphonic passages, frequent ink/pencil revisions, and poetic marginalia.

chopin_paris_stichvorlage.name: chopin_paris_stichvorlage
chopin_paris_stichvorlage.description: Frederic Chopin's delicate Parisian engraver's copy (Stichvorlage) with fine pointed nib, graceful slight right slant, small crisp oval noteheads, clean airy spacing, and pale cream wove paper.
chopin_paris_stichvorlage.paleography_notes: Based on Chopin's fair-copy Parisian Stichvorlagen prepared for Schlesinger and Brandus (NIFC facsimile corpus): fine pointed flexible steel nib yielding hairline precision, subtle rightward italic poise, small crisp oval noteheads leaving generous room for fioriture, ornate clefs, minimal barline overshoot, and pale cream French wove manuscript stock.

liszt_weimar_orchestral_draft.name: liszt_weimar_orchestral_draft
liszt_weimar_orchestral_draft.description: Franz Liszt's bold, sweeping Weimar orchestral score hand with large expressive strokes, exaggerated beams and barlines, generous margins, and dramatic ink pooling.
liszt_weimar_orchestral_draft.paleography_notes: Inspired by Liszt's Weimar symphonic-poem full-score drafts (1848-1861): expansive theatrical gesture across large-format multi-stave orchestral paper, broad high-contrast nib with heavy ink pooling at beam turns, large slash noteheads, exaggerated vertical barline overshoot, many blank pre-ruled staves for tacet instruments, and abundant orchestration/revision cues.

brahms_bold_vienna_autograph.name: brahms_bold_vienna_autograph
brahms_bold_vienna_autograph.description: Johannes Brahms's sturdy, thick-stemmed dark iron-gall Vienna autograph with robust teardrop noteheads, strong vertical barlines, and dense pre-ruled manuscript paper.
brahms_bold_vienna_autograph.paleography_notes: Reflects Brahms's mature Viennese autographs (symphonies, chamber works, and Klavierstucke): dense dark iron-gall ink on heavy pre-ruled Viennese/Breitkopf stock, sturdy thick stems with near-vertical posture, robust teardrop noteheads, disciplined economical measure packing that avoids wasted staves, and crisp classicizing clefs.
